cues.en: Now, another problem that we can solve using grid algorithm is fractional knapsack problem.
So here again let's look at first the problem statement.
Then we are going to explain it using the real life example.
So the problem statement says that given a set of items, each with a weight and value, determine the
number of each item to include in a collection so that the total weight is less than or equal to the
given limit.
So the total value is as large as possible.
So this problem often arises in resource allocation, where the decision maker have to choose the from
a set of non-divisible projects or tasks under a fixed budget or time constraint.
So you can consider a knapsack as a box, and this box has a limit of the utmost weight.
So let's make this clear in this example.
So let's say we have a three boxes like this.
And we have values and the weight of these boxes.
So we have to take only few items from this given item, such that the value of these items that we
put in the knapsack is maximum.
We cannot exceed the weight over here.
We need to get the maximum value.
So here we have an assumption that items can be broken down into fractions, so the capacity of our
knapsack is 50.
This means that we have to take only 50kg, but the value must be the maximum.
So if we take for example first two boxes.
So you see that the first box weight is 20 and the second box weight is 30.
So if you sum up them it's going to be 50.
And the value is going to be 220.
But this is not the maximum value that we can get.
So if we solve this using greedy algorithms the value is going to be 240.
So how can we get this.
So here the first thing that we will do we are going to calculate the ratio of the each box.
So we are doing it by putting the value divided by the weight.
So in this case 100 divided by 20 is five.
Then we are going to calculate it for this box which is four.
Then we are going to calculate for this box, which is six.
Then after doing so, we are going to order them based on the ratio in descending order.
So if you order them it's going to be like this.
So as we said the value is going to be 240.
So how do we get this after ordering this first we are taking the first one so we can take the this
box which is going to be ten kilograms and put it over here and we can take the second one.
So if we take first and second, in this case, the weight is going to be 30 and the remaining weight
is 20.
So 20 is less than the this box weight.
So this means that we have to take the some fraction from this box.
Now to be able to do that.
Here we have remaining weight which is 20.
And we have the ratio to calculate how much value we are going to take it, we have to multiply this
20 with four.
So we can take from here 80.
So 60 plus 100 plus 80 is going to be 240.
So here again this is a grid approach because at each step we are taking the current best solution and
adding it to the value.
And then we are continuing to the next step and in the next step also, we are taking the current best
solution and then we are adding all together to get the final solution.
So the code is going to be like this.
First we are going to create a class for each box over here, which is going to contain weight value
and ratio.
And the ratio is calculated by value divided by weight.
Then after doing so we are going to create the function like this.
So function will take as a parameter array of items and it's going to be the capacity.
So I'm going to put the array of the items over here where the objects of the class that we have created.
So we have inside weight value and ratio.
Then the first thing that we will do, we are going to sort this array based on the ratio in descending
order.
So in our case let's say as a capacity we are taking 50.
Then the next thing that we will do, we are going to order these elements inside the array based on
the ratio in descending order.
So when we order them it's going to be like this.
Then the next thing that we will do we are going to create used capacity which is going to be initially
zero.
Then the total value also initially is going to be zero.
Then we are going to loop through these items.
So the first item is this one.
So this means that we are going to check that if the used capacity plus the weight of this item is less
than the capacity.
So in our case the weight is ten and the used capacity is zero.
So zero plus ten is less than 50.
So this means that this if condition is true.
So we are going to continue over here.
And we are going to take the weight of this current item, which is ten, and add it to the used capacity
which is ten.
Then we are going to take the value of this item and add it to the total value.
So in our case the value is 60.
So we are going to add it over here.
Then we will continue to the next item.
Now the next item is the second one.
So here the weight is 20 and the used capacity is ten.
So ten plus 20 is 30 which is less than 50 which is the total capacity.
This means that this if condition is true we are going to continue to inside of this if condition,
and we are going to take the weight of the current item, which is 20, add it to the used weight,
which becomes the 30.
And similarly we are going to take the value, which is 100, and add it to the total value.
This becomes 160.
Then we are going to continue to the next item.
Now in the next item we have the third item.
So here we are going to check the safe conditions.
So the use capacity is 30 and the weight of current item is 30 which is greater than 50.
So in this case this condition is false which means that we are going to continue to the else part of
this if condition.
Now in the else part, we are going to create a new variable which is going to be unused weight.
So the unused weight is going to be calculated capacity minus used capacity which is 30.
So in this case it becomes 20.
Then we are going to take the fraction of the value from this item based on this unused weight and ratio.
So if we multiply unused weight with the ratio which is four, in this case it's going to become 80.
And we are going to add 80 to the total value.
This is going to become 240.
Then we are going to add the unused capacity.
So unused weight will be added to the unused capacity which is going to be 50.
Then we are going to put break over here.
Then at the end, we are just going to print out saying that the total value obtained is 240.
So that's how the fractional knapsack problem works.
So let's check this also in practice.
So here I have put the code that we have in the slide.
So first we are creating the item class in which we have the three properties weight value and ratio.
Then we are creating the function like this which takes two parameter items and capacity.
Then we are ordering the items based on the ratio in descending order.
Then we have two variables over here use capacity and total value.
Then we are looping through the items and based on this if condition calculating the value.
Then at the end we are just printing out the total value obtained to the console.
So here I have created three items that I have shown you before.
And based on these items we have created the items array.
Then we have called the knapsack method with items and with the capacity 50.
So if I run this, you will see that the obtained total value is 240.
So that's how we are solving the fractional knapsack problem using grid approach.
So hopefully everything is clear.
